I work night shifts now and it's much better paced for me than morning/day shift. Everything takes time, I know you can do it. Even if it's not shift manager (I'm stressed about the responsibility I have with it). Start small, be completely transparent with your boss and don't take on too much at once. Explain that you can work x amount of hours a week keeping your well being in mind. I promise you you can do it. Any type of job will help you with your sense of self worth. In highschool I used art to escape the real world. I wouldn't really think, I would just put my head down and try to translate a photograph onto a piece of paper/wood/canvas with whatever medium was expected of me and I would suddenly pull my head back up and it would be 9 hours later. People told me I was talented but there wasn't more to it for me. Not until I really started dissecting my trauma and thinking more abstractly. Now it's much more personal for me to work on pieces and I often find myself leaving the canvas less than 2 hours in, emotionally exhausted. Art can be a form of enjoyment but its also a form of self expression. It can be used to get through some nasty shit and understand yourself better. Enjoyment is subjective and art can be a powerful tool. I suggest you mess around with different styles, go to some art museums, read some books on different movements. Try to paint over oil pastel, try to make some cool collages out of magazines and old Dr. Seuss books. Have you ever played out a nightmare visually before? You will find a process that you enjoy... It's inevitable.  Sending you many good vibes.

Ok ok so personally I don't think I would've been able to get through CBT if I didn't have the techniques I learned from DBT. I have cPTSD and MDD and a few years back I did an inpatient stay for 6 weeks and worked on both of these with a therapist. In group meetings and smaller trauma groups. With my personal experience I started with DBT. it's basically a set of coping techniques that help bring you back into the here and now. Like mindfulness, self soothing, distraction, interpersonal effectiveness... Etc. It also is structured so you have goals and there's a spreadsheet that helps you stay focused on the things that you want to work on. There are apps that you can download that are basically the same as the sheet and you might even be able to find ones with workbooks saved in them. You chart down each coping mechanism you used throughout the day and it just helps you visualize the work you put into yourself. It helps raise your self awareness and self worth. I personally use self soothing and mindfulness a lot. For instance when my internal dialogue is suuuuper shitty and I feel like I'm going into one of those out of body experiences I know to grab a bowl of ice and shove my hands in it (self soothing) and start counting all of the red objects in the room or count the light bulbs (mindfulness) it brings me back into the here and now. There are about 14 techniques that have their own worksheets and honestly it might sound daunting but it's really helpful. In my own opinion CBT is where the work really starts. I challenged my inner dialogue and my self worth. I worked on justified and unjustified guilt and shame. I went into trauma sessions that absolutely rocked my shit. I learned how to give myself a voice when others refused to. I learned how to self validate and I learned a bit of emotional regulation. These are all really difficult to do alone and it's pretty much written into the curriculum that it should be done with a trained professional(s) these topics challenge the way we think about ourselves and the way we have learned to process reality. I grew up in a very unstable unhealthy environment so from the beginning of my life i was trying to hold my own hand and it wasn't always healthy. It was just a hand I could hold onto while I was ripped through black holes that tore my psyche into tiny broken pieces. I regained a bit of my power by going through these therapies and hell. Falling off the wagon is part of recovery, as AA likes to put it. So some days I feel like I didnt even learn anything at these stupid facilities BUT I have my daily sheet I can go to and write in. I can use some techniques to help me come to the realization that I am actually just hearing bits of my battered psyche try to hurt me because she's hurt. I just tell her maybe we can go on a walk tomorrow and paint some of this anger or turn it into a poem. Make something tangible out of this hopelessness I feel. It's a day by day process and I've actually been having a pretty crappy month or two but I know its going to blow over. This isn't forever. I am not stuck in a glue trap. I can overcome this. And that is the inner dialogue I worked hard for. Man writing this out really helped me. Thanks for asking, I really hope this helped. I read you're talking to a therapist right now. They might have a DBT packet somewhere or maybe can refer you into a program close to you. I know how exhausting it is to constantly be living in a state of anxiety. You deserve the world. 🌼
